Samir — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated PDF. We reviewed with legal and ops and put together a single proposed set of redlines (attached) to address your bullets. High-level summary below:

- Maintenance windows: propose "rolling maintenance" limited to two standard maintenance events per quarter per region; additionally we will establish a 72-hour scheduled maintenance notice and a one-time per-year blackout exception for declared financial close weeks (Redwood will not schedule non-emergency maintenance during customer-declared blackout weeks provided dates are shared 90 days in advance).

- Service credits calculation: propose region-scoped credits. If a single region experiences an Availability failure, credits apply to the billing units attributable to that region. For global incidents that require multi-region failover, credits will be applied pro rata by impacted region(s). We included a worked example in the redline.

- Response times: we can commit to 1-hour initial response for P1 (ack + first mitigation step), 4-hour target to have remediation plan, and P2 as 4-hour initial response / 24-hour remediation target. We flagged operational expectations (e.g., on-call escalation and required customer impact information) in the appendix.

- Credit cap: Redwood cannot accept a 50% monthly credit cap; propose a sliding cap that maxes at 30% monthly invoice for overlapping incidents with a 3-month aggregation safeguard to avoid runaway liability.

We attached "Redwood_proposed_SLA_redline.docx" with tracked changes. Laura — tagging you for legal wording and any procurement/contract risk concerns. Marissa — once we have legal sign-off can we route the final redline through DocuSign? I can also schedule a 30-minute alignment call with Pelion if they want to walk through examples.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Michael / Marissa — I reviewed Redwood's proposed redline and Pelion's asks. Below are suggested legal edits we should push back on versus accept; I've included exact clause language to drop into the MSA/Order Form to reduce back-and-forth.

1) Maintenance blackout language (accept with tightened notice):
"Customer may designate up to two (2) blackout periods per calendar year during which Provider shall not schedule any routine maintenance affecting Customer's provisioned region(s), provided Customer provides Provider with notice at least ninety (90) days in advance. Emergency maintenance required to address critical security or safety vulnerabilities shall remain excluded. Provider agrees to make commercially reasonable efforts to avoid scheduling routine maintenance during Customer-declared blackout weeks when possible."

2) Service Credit calculation (compromise):
"Service Credits shall be calculated on a per-region basis where the Impacted Region(s) are defined as the geographic region(s) identified in the Order Form. In multi-region incidents, Service Credits shall be apportioned pro rata to the billing units for each Impacted Region. The maximum aggregate Service Credits payable to Customer in any monthly billing period shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly invoice for the affected Account(s)."

3) Response times (accept with operational caveats):
"Provider will acknowledge P1 incidents within one (1) hour and provide an initial mitigation plan within four (4) hours. P2 incidents will receive an initial acknowledgement within four (4) hours and a remediation plan within twenty-four (24) hours. Acknowledgement and remediation commitments assume receipt of required diagnostic information and access requested by Provider."

4) Audit/evidence pack request (push to Ops):
We can commit to a quarterly uptime summary report and will provide a SOC2 attestation on request. We should not commit to full raw logs on an automated cadence — propose quarterly summary reports + on-request deeper evidence under a defined evidence request process.

Next steps: if the team agrees to the language above I can prepare a legal-ready redline (single file) to return to Pelion. Please confirm:
- Approve the 30% credit cap and pro rata regional allocation? (yes/no)
- Approve the blackout notice terms (90 days + 2 annual blackout periods)? (yes/no)
- Confirm we can offer quarterly summary reports and SOC2 attestation on request versus raw log delivery? (yes/no)

Laura Bennett
